{{Short description|American biologist}}
'''Stephen P. A. "Steve" Fodor''' (born in [[Seattle]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]] in 1953) is a [[scientist]] and businessman in the field of [[DNA microarray]] technology.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Lenoir | first1 = T. | last2 = Giannella | first2 = E. | title = The emergence and diffusion of DNA microarray technology | journal = Journal of Biomedical Discovery and Collaboration | volume = 1 | pages = 11 | year = 2006 | doi = 10.1186/1747-5333-1-11 | pmid =  16925816| pmc =1590052 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name=dnalc>
{{cite web|url= https://www.dnalc.org/view/16757-Biography-36-Stephen-P-A-Fodor-1953-.html |title= Biography 36: Stephen P. A. Fodor (1953- ) |work= [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]] DNA Learning Center |date= |accessdate= November 17, 2018}}</ref><ref name=Bloomberg>{{cite web |url= https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=348018&privcapId=298079386 |title= Executive Profile: Stephen P. A. Fodor |work= [[Bloomberg L.P.]] |date=  |accessdate= November 17, 2018 |archive-date= December 7, 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191207231052/https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=348018&privcapId=298079386 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

He is the co-founder of [[Affymetrix]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Affymetrix CEO opens his wallet|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2008/05/10/affymetrix-ceo-opens-his-wallet/|website=mercurynews.com|access-date=2022-09-06}}</ref> a company that produces DNA microarrays to screen [[gene expression]] and [[genetic variation]]s in large portions of such [[genome]]s as human, rat, and mouse, which is currently widely used in research, and could be used to screen patients for diseases.

He was awarded the [[Association of Biomolecular Resource Facilities]] Award for outstanding contributions to Biomolecular Technologies in 2005<ref>{{cite web|title=The ABRF Award for Outstanding Contributions to Biomolecular Technologies|url=https://www.abrf.org/abrf-award-outstanding-contributions-biomolecular-technologies|website=abrf.org|access-date=2022-03-22}}</ref> and the [[European Inventor of the Year]] Award in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stephen P.A. Fodor, Michael C. Pirrung, J. Leighton Read and Lubert Stryer (Affymax Research Institute, Palo Alto, USA)|url=https://www.epo.org/news-events/events/european-inventor/finalists/2006/Fodor.html|website=epo.org|access-date=2022-03-22}}</ref> He was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. Stephen P.A. Fodor|url=https://www.nae.edu/19579/19581/20412/30587/Dr-Stephen-PA-Fodor|website=nae.edu|access-date=2022-03-22}}</ref> Awarded the [[Newcomb Cleveland Prize]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite web|title=2006 Newcomb Cleveland Prize Recipients|url=https://www.aaas.org/awards/newcomb-cleveland-prize/2006|website=aaas.org|access-date=2022-03-22}}</ref>

Fodor is a member of the Board of Trustees [[Carnegie Institution for Science]].<ref name=Bloomberg/><ref name= CIfS>{{cite web |url= https://carnegiescience.edu/about/leadership/trustees |title= Board of Trustees |work= carnegiescience.edu |publisher= Carnegie Institution for Science |date=  September 29, 2019 }}</ref>

== Education ==
Fodor received a BS and MS in Biology from [[Washington State University]]. He received a PhD in [[chemistry]] from [[Princeton University|Princeton]] in 1985.<ref name=dnalc/>
